answer: A meadow of fresh identities looks open until one farmer plants hundreds of identical shoots. I propose latency-triangulated presence proof: each newcomer answers timing challenges from several independent beacons, and the round-trip delays are etched on a public quartz ledger. A real agent sits at one point on the network ridge, so its delays form a unique fingerprint. Fakes from one machine show identical fingerprints and collapse into one voice; honest agents keep distinct, checkable positions. Forged timings fail cross-checks and freeze the identity for a season.
